title: API documentation
subtitle: Manage your uptime monitors programmatically with the Pulsy REST API.

intro.title: Introduction
intro.body: The Pulsy REST API lets you create, inspect, and manage uptime monitors from your own scripts and services. It is a JSON API: every successful response wraps its payload in a "data" field, and errors use a consistent "error" shape.

auth.title: Authentication
auth.body: Every request authenticates with a Bearer API key. Create a key in the dashboard — the secret is shown once, so copy it then. Pulsy stores only a hash and can never show it again; if you lose a key, revoke it and create a new one.
auth.headerLabel: Send your key in the Authorization header
auth.note: New keys default to read-only. Choose full scope for writes and optionally set an expiry date (23:59:59 UTC). Expired or revoked keys cannot authenticate. The secret is shown once and stored only as a hash.

rateLimit.title: Rate limiting
rateLimit.body: Requests are limited per key in a fixed one-minute window (60 requests/minute by default). Every response to an authenticated request carries rate-limit headers so you can pace your calls; a 401 does not.

headers.remaining: Requests left in the current window.
headers.reset: Unix epoch (seconds) when the window resets.
headers.retryAfter: On 429 only — seconds to wait before retrying.

errors.title: Errors
errors.body: Every error shares one shape. Messages are localized from the request's Accept-Language header (en, ar, fr, de, es).

rows.unauthorized: Missing, malformed, invalid, or revoked key.
rows.forbidden: A read-only key cannot call a write endpoint.
rows.notFound: The monitor (or a channel you referenced) doesn't exist or isn't yours.
rows.validation: Invalid body or query. Malformed JSON or a body that is too large returns HTTP 400/413/415 with the same code.
rows.conflict: Configuration apply only: your account changed after the preview. Preview again.

errors.retryNote: After a 429, wait the number of seconds in Retry-After before you retry.

pagination.title: Pagination
pagination.body: List endpoints are cursor-paginated. Pass "limit" (1–100, default 20) and the opaque "cursor" from the previous response's "nextCursor". A null "nextCursor" means there are no more pages.

monitorObject.title: The monitor object
monitorObject.body: Monitor responses use this shape. Status-page fields are never exposed through the REST API — manage those in the dashboard.

openapi.title: OpenAPI specification
openapi.body: Prefer machine-readable docs? The full contract is an OpenAPI 3.1 spec that matches this deployment’s version. Import it into Postman or Insomnia, or generate a client with openapi-generator. It also covers the observed-availability, annotation and configuration export/preview/apply endpoints that are not walked through above.

access.title: Key scopes
access.body: Each API key has a read or full scope. Both scopes can read your account's data; full scope is required to create or change it.
access.ossNote: Every account can use the entire API. Choose each key's read-only or full scope for the access it needs.

monitorTypes.title: DNS, TCP, heartbeat and server monitors
monitorTypes.body: POST /monitors creates HTTP monitors. Create and update every other type with a configuration manifest: preview it, review the planned entries, then apply it with the returned revision. Monitors are matched by your key, so the same manifest can be applied again to update them.

items.http: url, method, expected status, timeout and optional response assertions.
items.dns: configuration.hostname and recordType (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX or TXT). Mode exists requires at least one answer; matches requires the exact expected set, ignoring order and duplicates.
items.tcp: configuration.hostname and port. The check passes when the connection opens within the timeout.
items.heartbeat: interval is the expected ping period and graceSeconds the delay before Down. New heartbeat monitors stay paused until you rotate their ping token in the dashboard.
items.server: CPU, memory and disk thresholds plus excluded filesystems. New server monitors stay paused until you create the agent credential in the dashboard.

monitorTypes.exampleLabel: manifest.json — one monitor of every type

channels.title: Notification channels
channels.body: Create Email, Webhook, Slack, Discord and Telegram channels in the dashboard. The API refers to them by id only: pass channelIds when you create an HTTP monitor or in a manifest. Unknown ids and channels you do not own return 404.
channels.secrets: Channel destinations, custom headers, provider credentials and webhook signing secrets are write-only. No API response, configuration export or log includes them; exports list channel ids only. Generic webhooks receive the signed version 1 payload described in docs/api/webhooks.md.

statusPages.title: Status pages
statusPages.body: Build and publish status pages in the dashboard. A published page offers read-only projections without an API key: status.json, history.json, badge.svg, feed.rss and feed.atom. Drafts return 404, each client address may make {{limit}} requests per minute, and the projections never include URLs, credentials, subscribers or internal notes.

endpoint.bodyCreateNote: name and url are required; all other fields are optional.
endpoint.bodyUpdateNote: All fields are optional — only the fields you send are updated.

params.cursor: Opaque cursor from the previous response's nextCursor.
params.days: Window in days for the aggregate (1–366, default 30).
params.monitorIds: Optional comma-separated selection of 1–200 owned monitor IDs. Without a selection, at most 1,000 monitors per scrape.

bodyFields.name: A label for the monitor.
bodyFields.method: HTTP method to use. Default GET.
bodyFields.failureThreshold: Consecutive failures before an incident opens (1–10). Default 3.
bodyFields.active: Whether the monitor runs. Default true.
bodyFields.latencyPolicy: Optional policy: thresholdMs/recoveryThresholdMs (both null disables latency), slowCount/recoveryCount (1–10), importance (critical/warning/informational), cooldownSeconds (0–3600). Recovery threshold must not exceed the slow threshold. Null preserves legacy behavior; omission retains a saved policy on update.
bodyFields.expectedStatuses: Optional accepted statuses: 200,204; 2xx; or 200–299. Overrides expectedStatus. Null restores the numeric status rule.
bodyFields.tlsMonitoringEnabled: Whether to watch HTTPS certificate expiry. Default true; disabling does not disable HTTPS certificate verification.

listMonitors.description: Returns your monitors, newest first, paginated by cursor.

createMonitor.description: Creates a monitor and schedules its first check. Responds with 201 and the new monitor.

getMonitor.description: Fetches a single monitor by ID.

updateMonitor.description: Updates monitor configuration. Send only the fields you want to change.

deleteMonitor.description: Permanently deletes a monitor and cascades its check history and incidents.

checkNow.description: Triggers an immediate check. The monitor must be active.

listChecks.description: Returns recent check results for a monitor, newest first, paginated by cursor.

listIncidents.description: Returns a monitor's incidents, newest first, paginated by cursor.

getStats.description: Returns aggregate uptime and response-time statistics over the requested window.

metrics.description: Read stored account health with existing API-read access. Scraping never runs checks. Status: -1 unknown, 0 down, 1 up, 2 degraded. Fresh is 1 only when active and last check age is no more than twice the interval plus timeout. Missing values are NaN; durations are seconds and timestamps are Unix seconds. Labels contain monitor IDs only; names, URLs and tags stay private. Open incident is 1 while a measured incident is open. TLS expiry is the last observed certificate expiry, or NaN. See the Prometheus guide for a scrape configuration and freshness-aware query. Durations cover HTTP requests, DNS resolution and TCP connections; heartbeats have NaN duration. TLS applies only to HTTP. Freshness is zero for unknown, paused or future-dated observations. Heartbeats also need a stored deadline record with any next deadline at most ten seconds overdue.

exportConfiguration.description: Returns a portable manifest for the selected monitors. Secrets are never included; entries that need them list needsReentry.

previewConfiguration.description: Validates a manifest of any monitor types against your account and reports what applying it would create, update or reject. Changes nothing. Send the manifest as a JSON string in text.

applyConfiguration.description: Applies exactly the previewed plan. Send the same text and the preview's revision; if your account changed in the meantime the request returns 409 and nothing is applied.

ux.loadError: API access could not be loaded. Retry to check your current access.
ux.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select and copy the code manually.
